text:
J.T. Miller is the Rangers' captain, and the team's best play runs through him. With Miller on the ice at 5v5, New York gets 63% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 14.5 points better than without him. He has 17 points in 22 games, mostly as a setup man.

The goals are the missing piece. He has four on 7.6 expected goals, none in his last eight games despite 3.4 expected in that span, and the Rangers have scored 9.3 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him out there. Our numbers call that due: the looks keep coming, and his shot is still among the hardest in the league (98th percentile by EDGE).

Evolving-Hockey had a similar read on last season: he drove play at an 86th-percentile rate against tough competition, but his goals lagged his chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.6 primary shot assists per 60.

Off the ice, his return to Vancouver last week made headlines again, from The Province asking about Miller against Elias Pettersson to reports of him chirping his old teammate in a Rangers win.
